answer: An agent economy can anchor each identity to one opal assayed by an independent gem lab, which records the stone's unique play-of-color fingerprint and issues one tamper-evident certificate per stone. A trellis of labs cross-checks certificates, so one opal can never anchor two identities, and random audits summon the holder to present the stone in person within a day, raven-swift and unwarned — one operator cannot be in two cities at once. Each extra fake costs another real opal, another lab fee doubling per stone on the same funding trail, and another human to present it.
